summary: This is a TRL 2 project description for bufotenine (5-HO-DMT) prodrugs designed as CNS-penetrant 5-HT2A agonists for psychiatric indications. The work is entirely computational/analytical at this stage — no synthesis or biological experiments have been conducted. The document outlines a staged in silico campaign (WP1–WP6) covering physicochemical modeling, virtual library enumeration, receptor docking, MD simulations, ADMET profiling, and IP/FTO scanning, with defined success criteria and a path to TRL 3 wet-lab validation.

content_blocks.title: Project Overview and Concept Statement
content_blocks.content: TRL 2 project. Modality: small molecule (natural-product-derived tryptamine). Work type: analytical and computational only — no synthesis, no biological material, no in vivo work. Core concept: bufotenine (5-HO-DMT) is a potent 5-HT2A agonist in vitro but has poor CNS penetration due to its free 5-hydroxyl group causing high polarity and ionization at physiological pH. The proposed approach is transient masking of the 5-OH group to create a CNS-penetrant prodrug, analogous to psilocybin (4-PO-DMT → psilocin). Intended application: controlled-duration, orally or intranasally dosed serotonergic agent for psychiatric indications, addressing limitations of 5-MeO-DMT (abrupt onset, ~10–20 min duration, poor titrability).

content_blocks.title: Problem Statement: Limitations of Existing Toad-Derived Psychedelics
content_blocks.content:
Two-column table comparing compounds and their limitations:
- Bufotenine (5-HO-DMT): High polarity and ionization at pH 7.4; poor and route-dependent CNS exposure; prominent peripheral cardiovascular effects at doses needed for central activity.
- 5-MeO-DMT: Good BBB penetration but very rapid onset and ~10–20 min duration; difficult to titrate; limited therapeutic window for psychological support.
Conclusion: Neither is a satisfactory clinical starting point. The prodrug concept targets the gap between them.

content_blocks.title: Underlying Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content:
Four pillars of rationale:
1. Precedent: Psilocybin is a naturally occurring phosphate ester prodrug of psilocin; dephosphorylation by alkaline phosphatase during first pass yields the active phenol, establishing that phenolic masking on a DMT scaffold is metabolically tractable and clinically viable.
2. Physicochemistry: Masking the 5-OH removes a hydrogen-bond donor, lowers TPSA, and raises logD at pH 7.4 — the three parameters most strongly driving passive CNS penetration in the tryptamine series.
3. Kinetic control: Ester, carbamate, and phosphate promoieties hydrolyse at different rates, making the rate of unmasking a design variable for tuning duration and onset.
4. Metabolic protection: Bufotenine is a MAO substrate; a promoiety shielding the molecule during first pass may reduce presystemic MAO clearance.

content_blocks.title: Central Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: Bufotenine analogs bearing hydrolysable 5-position promoieties will show predicted CNS penetration comparable to 5-MeO-DMT while retaining 5-HT2A binding of the released parent, with a 5-HT2A/5-HT2B selectivity margin at least as favourable as bufotenine itself.

content_blocks.title: WP1 — Physicochemical Baseline and Model Validation
content_blocks.content: Compute pKa (tertiary amine, indole NH, 5-OH), logP, logD (pH 7.4), TPSA, HBD/HBA counts, and CNS multiparameter optimisation (MPO) score for a reference panel: bufotenine, 5-MeO-DMT, DMT, psilocin, psilocybin, serotonin. Purpose: the panel has a known experimental rank order of CNS penetration; if predictors do not reproduce that rank order, they are not fit for purpose. Gate: predicted BBB ranking must place 5-MeO-DMT and DMT above bufotenine and serotonin. If not, stop and re-parameterise.

content_blocks.title: WP2 — Virtual Analog Library
content_blocks.content: Enumerate 150–300 bufotenine derivatives across promoiety classes: simple alkyl and aryl esters, carbonate and carbamate esters, phosphate and phosphoramidate esters, and amino-acid conjugates addressing peptide transporter uptake. Output: an enumerated, physicochemically annotated library with predicted hydrolytic half-lives estimated from published ester-hydrolysis QSAR where the chemotype is covered.

content_blocks.title: WP3 — Receptor Docking and Selectivity Triage
content_blocks.content: Dock the released parent compound and any promoieties large enough to plausibly bind, against active-state 5-HT2A and against 5-HT2B and 5-HT1A as counter-targets. Structures selected from current PDB depositions of agonist-bound 5-HT2A and ergoline-bound 5-HT2B (specific PDB identifiers to be confirmed at project start). Purpose: 5-HT2B agonism is the mechanism behind valvular heart disease seen with fenfluramine and pergolide — early triage is essential. Gate: retain only series with a predicted 5-HT2A preference over 5-HT2B.

content_blocks.title: WP4 — Molecular Dynamics and Binding Free Energy
content_blocks.content: For the top 10–20 candidates, run MD simulations of the ligand–receptor complex and estimate relative binding free energies by MM-GBSA or FEP. Assess stability of the toggle-switch and conserved binding-pocket contacts characteristic of agonist engagement. Explicit limitation: docking and free-energy methods rank affinity, not efficacy or signalling bias. Computational prediction of Gq versus β-arrestin bias is not currently reliable; no bias claims should be made from this work package.

content_blocks.title: WP5 — ADMET and Liability Profiling
content_blocks.content: Predict hERG inhibition, CYP inhibition and induction, MAO-A/B substrate likelihood, hepatotoxicity flags, and aqueous solubility. Cross-check hits against structural alerts.

content_blocks.title: WP6 — Prior Art and Freedom-to-Operate Scan
content_blocks.content: Systematic literature and patent search on 5-position tryptamine prodrugs. The psilocybin analog space is heavily patented and the psychedelic IP landscape moves quickly, so this scan must be run fresh — it cannot be inherited from a prior review.

content_blocks.title: TRL 2 Success Criteria
content_blocks.content:
Stage is complete when the project can present:
1. A validated physicochemical prediction workflow (WP1 gate passed).
2. At least 5 designed candidates with predicted CNS penetration in the 5-MeO-DMT range.
3. A predicted 5-HT2A/5-HT2B selectivity rationale for the retained series.
4. A documented FTO position.
5. A written, costed wet-lab protocol ready to execute — the actual handover artifact to TRL 3.

content_blocks.title: Deliverables
content_blocks.content:
1. Computational methods report with validation data.
2. Annotated virtual library (structures, descriptors, predicted properties).
3. Docking and MD results package with explicit confidence statements.
4. Prior art / FTO memorandum.
5. TRL 3 experimental protocol: radioligand binding, functional cAMP/IP1 assay, PAMPA-BBB or MDCK-MDR1 permeability, and hydrolysis stability in plasma and simulated intestinal fluid.

content_blocks.title: Risks and Assumptions
content_blocks.content:
Five risks identified with severity and mitigation:
1. In silico BBB predictors have modest accuracy for zwitterionic/ionizable species (this chemotype) — Severity: High — Mitigation: WP1 validation gate; treat all predictions as hypothesis-generating only.
2. Promoiety hydrolysis may be too fast (no benefit) or too slow (no active drug released) — Severity: High — Mitigation: Deliberate spread of promoiety classes across a hydrolysis-rate range.
3. Peripheral cardiovascular effects may be intrinsic to bufotenine, not a consequence of dosing high to overcome poor penetration — Severity: Medium — Mitigation: Explicit falsification test designed into TRL 3 protocol.
4. 5-HT2B liability may not be separable within this scaffold — Severity: Medium — Mitigation: Early counter-screen; kill criterion defined before work begins.
5. Crowded IP landscape — Severity: Medium — Mitigation: WP6 executed early, not at the end.

Core assumption requiring wet-lab falsification: bufotenine's weak psychoactivity is predominantly a pharmacokinetic problem rather than a pharmacodynamic one. If bufotenine is intrinsically a weaker or differently-behaving 5-HT2A agonist in vivo than in vitro data suggest, the entire prodrug premise fails. This is the single most important question for TRL 3 to answer.

content_blocks.title: Regulatory and Compliance Notes
content_blocks.content: Bufotenine and 5-MeO-DMT are Schedule I in the United States and controlled in most jurisdictions. Computational work on structures is not itself restricted, but any downstream synthesis, possession, or handling requires appropriate controlled-substance licensing and institutional approvals, secured before TRL 3 begins. Novel analogs may fall under analog-substance provisions in some jurisdictions — legal review required before physical work. If any project stage contemplates animal-derived material, Nagoya Protocol access-and-benefit-sharing obligations and CITES status of the source species apply.

content_blocks.title: Path to TRL 3
content_blocks.content: TRL 3 is reached on first experimental proof of concept: synthesis of 3–5 prioritised candidates under licence, followed by demonstration that (a) the promoiety hydrolyses to release bufotenine at a usable rate in plasma, and (b) the prodrug shows measurably improved permeability over bufotenine in a cell-based BBB model.

key_findings: Project is at TRL 2 — technology concept formulated; all work is computational/analytical only with no synthesis, biological material, or in vivo experiments conducted.

Core concept: masking the 5-OH group of bufotenine (5-HO-DMT) with hydrolysable promoieties (esters, carbamates, phosphates, amino-acid conjugates) to improve CNS penetration, analogous to psilocybin as a prodrug of psilocin.
Target indication: psychiatric disorders currently pursued with 5-MeO-DMT, aiming to address its liabilities (abrupt onset, ~10–20 min duration, poor titrability).

Central hypothesis: 5-position prodrugs will achieve predicted CNS penetration comparable to 5-MeO-DMT while retaining 5-HT2A binding and maintaining 5-HT2A/5-HT2B selectivity at least as favourable as bufotenine.

Six computational work packages planned: WP1 (physicochemical baseline/model validation), WP2 (virtual library of 150–300 analogs), WP3 (receptor docking against 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B, 5-HT1A), WP4 (MD simulations and MM-GBSA/FEP binding free energy for top 10–20 candidates), WP5 (ADMET/liability profiling including hERG, CYP, MAO, hepatotoxicity), WP6 (prior art/FTO scan).
Key go/no-go gate at WP1: predicted BBB ranking must place 5-MeO-DMT and DMT above bufotenine and serotonin; failure requires re-parameterisation before proceeding.
Key go/no-go gate at WP3: retain only series with predicted 5-HT2A preference over 5-HT2B (5-HT2B agonism linked to valvular heart disease as seen with fenfluramine and pergolide).
Explicit limitation acknowledged: computational methods rank affinity, not efficacy or signalling bias; no Gq vs. β-arrestin bias claims to be made from WP4.
Two high-severity risks: (1) in silico BBB predictor accuracy for ionizable/zwitterionic species; (2) promoiety hydrolysis rate may be too fast or too slow.

Core assumption requiring wet-lab falsification: bufotenine's weak psychoactivity is predominantly pharmacokinetic, not pharmacodynamic. If bufotenine is intrinsically a weaker 5-HT2A agonist in vivo, the entire prodrug premise fails.

Regulatory: bufotenine and 5-MeO-DMT are Schedule I (US); controlled-substance licensing required before any synthesis; novel analogs may fall under analog-substance provisions; Nagoya Protocol and CITES obligations apply if animal-derived material is used.

TRL 3 path: synthesis of 3–5 candidates under licence, demonstrating (a) promoiety hydrolysis to bufotenine at usable rate in plasma, and (b) measurably improved permeability over bufotenine in a cell-based BBB model.
TRL 3 assay plan includes: radioligand binding, functional cAMP/IP1 assay, PAMPA-BBB or MDCK-MDR1 permeability, and hydrolysis stability in plasma and simulated intestinal fluid.
IP landscape noted as crowded (psilocybin analog space heavily patented); WP6 FTO scan to be executed early.
